summary: AI observability has become a critical discipline as LLM deployments scale in complexity and cost, with the market growing to an estimated $2.69 billion in 2026 and projected to reach $9.26 billion by 2030 at a 36.2% CAGR. Without proper monitoring, teams fly blind on prompt performance, token spend, latency regressions, and failure modes that compound quickly at production scale. Gartner predicts that by 2028, LLM observability investments will account for 50% of all GenAI deployments, up from just 15% in early 2026, underscoring how central these tools have become to responsible AI operations.

tools.name: LangSmith
tools.monitors: LLM traces, chain execution steps, prompt inputs and outputs, evaluation runs, and agent reasoning steps within LangChain and LangGraph workflows
features: Deep LangChain and LangGraph integration with automatic trace capture
Rich debugging interface with step-by-step chain inspection
Built-in evaluation framework with human and automated scoring
Dataset management for regression testing and fine-tuning
Prompt versioning and comparison across experiments
Annotation queues for human review workflows
Team collaboration and project-level organization
tools.pricing: Developer tier free at 5,000 traces per month; Plus at $39 per seat per month with overage around $2.50 per thousand traces at standard retention; Enterprise pricing available on request. Approximately £80 per month for 100K requests on paid tiers.
tools.best_for: Teams building with LangChain or LangGraph who need a deeply integrated debugging and evaluation environment with strong human-in-the-loop review capabilities

tools.name: Helicone
tools.monitors: LLM API requests and responses, token usage, cost per request, latency, error rates, and model-level spend across providers including OpenAI, Anthropic, and others
features: Proxy-based integration requiring minimal code changes — typically 2-minute setup
Real-time cost tracking and spend dashboards by model, user, and endpoint
Request caching to reduce redundant API calls and cut costs
Rate limiting and access control at the gateway level
Prompt templates and versioning with A/B testing support
User-level usage segmentation for SaaS cost attribution
Open-source and self-hostable with SOC-2 Type II and HIPAA on Team tier
tools.pricing: Free Hobby tier at 10K requests per month; Pro at $79 per month with unlimited seats and usage-based overages; Team at $799 per month adding SOC-2 Type II and HIPAA compliance; custom Enterprise pricing with SAML SSO and on-premises deployment. Approximately £20 per month for 100K requests, making it the most cost-effective managed option.
tools.best_for: Teams that prioritize cost visibility and optimization with minimal integration overhead, particularly those running high request volumes across multiple LLM providers and needing granular spend attribution

tools.name: Weights & Biases (W&B Weave)
tools.monitors: LLM traces, experiment runs, model evaluations, dataset versions, prompt performance, and full ML training pipelines alongside LLM-specific observability
features: Unified platform covering both traditional ML experiment tracking and LLM tracing
Weave module for LLM call tracing, evaluation, and iteration
Rich experiment comparison with interactive dashboards
Dataset and artifact versioning with lineage tracking
Evaluation pipelines with custom and built-in scorers
Collaborative reports for sharing findings across teams
Integrations with major ML frameworks and LLM providers
tools.pricing: Free tier available for individuals; Teams plan at $50 per user per month; Enterprise pricing on request. Storage and compute overages apply on higher tiers. Pricing details for Weave-specific LLM features follow the broader W&B subscription model.
tools.best_for: ML and AI teams that run both traditional model training and LLM workloads who want a single platform for experiment tracking, dataset management, and LLM observability without switching between tools

tools.name: Arize AI
tools.monitors: LLM traces, embeddings, retrieval quality in RAG pipelines, model performance drift, hallucination signals, and enterprise-scale telemetry across structured and unstructured AI systems
features: Phoenix open-source tracing library for local and cloud deployment
Enterprise telemetry with OpenTelemetry-native instrumentation
RAG pipeline monitoring including retrieval relevance and chunk quality scoring
Embedding drift detection and cluster analysis for semantic shift
LLM evaluation with built-in and custom evaluators
Integrations with LlamaIndex, LangChain, and major LLM providers
Long-standing ML monitoring capabilities extended to generative AI
tools.pricing: Arize Phoenix is open-source and free to self-host. The managed Arize platform uses enterprise pricing with custom quotes; a free developer tier is available for Phoenix Cloud. Full enterprise contracts typically start in the tens of thousands annually depending on volume and features.
tools.best_for: Enterprise teams with complex RAG architectures or hybrid ML and LLM systems that need production-grade telemetry, embedding analysis, and compliance-ready monitoring at scale

tools.name: Langfuse
tools.monitors: LLM traces, prompt versions, user sessions, token usage, latency, evaluation scores, and cost across multi-step LLM pipelines and agentic workflows
features: Open-source with self-hosted option for full data control
Detailed trace and span visualization for complex multi-step pipelines
Prompt management with versioning and rollback capabilities
Online and offline evaluation with LLM-as-judge and human scoring
Dataset creation from production traces for continuous improvement
SDKs for Python, JavaScript, and TypeScript with broad framework support
Native OpenTelemetry support for standardized instrumentation
tools.pricing: Langfuse Cloud free tier available for under 50K requests per month at no cost; paid cloud plans start at approximately £20 for 500K requests. Self-hosted version is free with infrastructure costs estimated around £30 per month plus approximately 2 hours of maintenance per month. Enterprise cloud pricing available on request.
tools.best_for: Teams wanting open-source tracing with strong prompt management and evaluation capabilities, especially those who need self-hosted deployment for data privacy or compliance and want a cost-effective alternative to proprietary tools

tools.name: OpenLLMetry
tools.monitors: LLM API calls, token consumption, latency, and trace context across LLM providers and frameworks using OpenTelemetry-native instrumentation
features: OpenTelemetry-native SDK that emits standard OTLP traces and metrics
Auto-instrumentation for OpenAI, Anthropic, Cohere, LangChain, LlamaIndex, and others
Vendor-agnostic design allowing export to any OpenTelemetry-compatible backend
Minimal code changes required — typically a single initialization call
Span attributes aligned with emerging LLM semantic conventions
Works alongside existing observability stacks without replacing them
Open-source under Apache 2.0 with active community development by Traceloop
tools.pricing: Fully open-source and free to use. Backend storage and visualization costs depend entirely on the destination observability platform chosen (e.g., Grafana, Honeycomb, Datadog, or self-hosted Jaeger). No per-request or per-seat fees from OpenLLMetry itself.
tools.best_for: Engineering teams with an existing OpenTelemetry observability stack who want to add LLM-specific tracing without adopting a new dedicated platform, or those building a vendor-neutral instrumentation layer that can route to multiple backends

tools.name: Confident AI (DeepEval)
tools.monitors: LLM output quality, hallucination, answer relevancy, faithfulness, bias, toxicity, and 50+ research-backed evaluation metrics across development and production pipelines
features: 50+ research-backed metrics open-sourced through DeepEval including G-Eval, RAG faithfulness, and contextual relevancy
Online evaluations integrated directly into the observability layer
Regression testing suite to catch quality degradation across prompt or model changes
Real-time production monitoring with automatic evaluation on live traffic
Dataset management for curating golden test sets from production data
Used by teams at OpenAI, Google, and Microsoft for evaluation workflows
CI/CD integration for evaluation-gated deployments
tools.pricing: DeepEval is open-source and free. Confident AI managed platform offers a free tier; paid plans scale with evaluation volume and team size. Enterprise pricing available on request for production-scale deployments with SLA support.
tools.best_for: Teams for whom output quality and safety evaluation is the primary concern, particularly those building RAG systems or customer-facing AI applications that require rigorous, metrics-driven quality gates before and after deployment

cost_tips: Implement prompt caching and request deduplication at the gateway level — tools like Helicone offer built-in caching that can eliminate redundant API calls for repeated or near-identical queries, with some teams reporting 20-40% cost reductions on cache-heavy workloads without any change to application logic.

Right-size your model selection by routing requests based on complexity: use smaller, cheaper models such as GPT-4o mini or Claude Haiku for simple classification or extraction tasks, and reserve frontier models for genuinely complex reasoning — observability tools that log per-request metadata make it straightforward to identify which request types are over-engineered and can be safely downgraded.

Set token budgets and enforce output length constraints explicitly in your system prompts and API parameters, since many LLM cost overruns come from unexpectedly verbose completions — monitoring tools that track token distribution per endpoint help identify which prompts are generating disproportionately long outputs that could be capped with a max_tokens limit or a more directive system instruction.

Use trace data from your observability platform to identify high-latency, high-cost pipeline steps and evaluate whether retrieval chunk sizes, context window usage, or redundant tool calls can be reduced — in RAG systems specifically, trimming irrelevant retrieved chunks before they enter the prompt context can cut input token counts significantly while often improving answer quality by reducing noise.
